Trudging through the coastal shallows, the trawlauth looks to be merely the head of a thick trailing fog that drowns out all life behind 
it. When in reality, it is performing a vital service to the ocean floor by scraping off the virulent oxygen sucking algae and clearing space 
for new plant and coral growth. Th rough symbiotic mutualism the trawlauth is host to a colony of bacteria that resides on and under 
its exoskeleton. Living off the excrement of the crustacean and leaching calcium from its shell, the bacteria builds up funnels along the 
back of the creature. Th rough these, it vents a viscous bacterial soup that billows out into the water in thick, gill-choking clouds that 
protects the trawlauth from any nearby predators while spreading its bacterial spores far and wide.
